clue.text: European paper with story about Corbyn?

indicators.note: the story goes round, so the earlier pieces sit inside it

parts.note: a story can be a falsehood
the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A European newspaper runs a piece about the former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Corbyn, a former Labour Party leader, is a well-known British socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Corbyn is an example of a socialist, informally called a leftie; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Third member dropped from team of Brownies?

indicators.note: the word for a team loses the item standing third in its line of letters

parts.note: a football or cricket side has this many players

explanation.surface: A Brownie pack has had to leave out its third member.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are junior Girl Guides in the surface, but in folklore a brownie is a household elf.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a small helpful elf of folklore, so something belonging to brownies is elven.

clue.text: Fish sandwich you can get in America

definitions.text: sandwich you can get in America
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a long filled roll, also called a sub or hoagie

explanation.surface: A fish sandwich available in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one fish sandwich; actually it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The electric ray is called a torpedo, and in parts of the US a long submarine-style sandwich goes by that name too.

clue.text: Assessed a valet due to be reassigned

indicators.note: reassigning means putting into new positions, so these letters get a new order

explanation.surface: A manservant's performance was reviewed because he was about to be moved to other duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to judge its worth, which is what evaluating means.

clue.text: One after bananas or giant pasta shapes

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between bananas and huge pasta tubes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One after' puts I at the end of the mixed-up letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni are short ridged tubes, one of the many named shapes of Italian dried pasta.

clue.text: Ciabatta German packs up for sports meet

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top
the phrase packs the letters inside itself, carried across the word break

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A German packing bread rolls for a sports meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat races, so it is a sporting event on water.

clue.text: Looked stupidly good, like Batman without a top?

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

explanation.surface: Someone looking very fine, like Batman but shirtless.
explanation.walkthrough: Batman wears a cape, so he is caped; beheaded, that leaves APED, after G.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed in a vacant or astonished way, so gaped means stared stupidly.

clue.text: People in authority taking charge in treatment

indicators.note: the people take something in, so it goes inside them

parts.note: the unnamed powers that be, as in 'they say'
a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: Officials taking control of someone's medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment meant to heal a disorder, physical or mental.

clue.text: Without a hooter to squeeze one might be thus

definitions.text: Without a hooter to squeeze one might be thus

indicators.note: squeezing something presses it in, so a letter goes inside

explanation.surface: If you had no horn to squeeze, you would make no sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter means both a car horn and a nose. Read whole, the clue describes the answer: with no horn to honk you would be silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no horn to sound makes no sound at all, which is exactly what silent or soundless describes.

clue.text: Done with husband, a half-cut dung beetle

indicators.note: half of the word is cut away, keeping only its back half

explanation.surface: A dung beetle is finished with its husband, and the speaker is half-drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' (British slang for tipsy) and 'dung beetle' tempt you to read beetle as the insect; it is a verb. Beetling brows jut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle is to jut out or project, as cliffs or eyebrows do, which is what overhanging means.

clue.text: Conductor's leg broken by vicar

indicators.note: the leg is broken open and something is set inside it

parts.note: short for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.surface: An orchestra conductor's leg fractured by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. André Previn conducted the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: André Previn was a famous conductor and composer, music director of several major orchestras.

clue.text: One accepting about query not being answered

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: standard abbreviation for question or query

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a question that no one ever responds to.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrequited love is not returned; the word means unreturned or unanswered in feeling.

clue.text: Bar and bench losing their heads once again

indicators.note: each word sheds its first letter, its head

explanation.surface: A pub's counter and seating being beheaded all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar and bench both suggest the law courts, but here they are a ban and a pew.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something anew means starting it over again, fresh, a second time.

clue.text: Perhaps a jolly solver entertained by short escort

indicators.note: a guest entertained is held within the host's company
cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a partner on an evening out
the solver is the person being addressed

explanation.surface: A cheerful puzzler taken out by a brief companion.
explanation.walkthrough: A jolly is British slang for a pleasure trip or outing, often at someone else's expense.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolly is an outing for fun, and a day out is one example of such a trip.

clue.text: Investments in iTunes Anonymous disrupted

indicators.note: disruption throws things out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Money put into Apple's music store, with a hacking group causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity is a financial product bought with a lump sum that pays out regular income, a kind of investment.

clue.text: Learn, say, about Freud?

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or astir, so these letters are moved round

explanation.surface: A prompt to study, perhaps, what Freud thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual by-example marker, but it is part of the fodder; the question mark does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud founded psychoanalysis, so he is an example of a psychoanalyst, often shortened to analyst or analyser.

clue.text: A pad fit to house cunning people

definitions.note: includes the article: an apartment is a pad

indicators.note: housing something means holding it inside

parts.note: art can mean craft or guile

explanation.surface: A flat suitable for crafty folk to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad is informal slang for a flat or place to live, so an apartment is a pad.

clue.text: Sharp tenor dressed in fabulous net hood

indicators.note: something dressed in clothing sits inside it
fabulous suggests something fantastic and made up, so these letters are reinvented

explanation.surface: A smart singer wearing a gorgeous mesh hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' looks like a description of the tenor's dress; it is the definition, as in 'at three sharp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp after a time means exactly at it, so 'on the dot' and 'sharp' are synonymous idioms.

clue.text: Hard right-winger supporting one's record

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports another piece is placed below it

parts.note: standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A hardline conservative backing someone's track record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard right-winger' reads as one phrase but splits: H is separate from the Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: A history is an account or record of past events, as in a medical history.

clue.text: Time article about international view of Lhasa?

indicators.note: the outer pieces go around the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: my bet is, meaning in my view

explanation.surface: A magazine piece giving a world perspective on the Tibetan capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time article' together is the outer pair, and 'about' wraps them around the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, so something from Lhasa is Tibetan, defined by example.

clue.text: Small current on a chat server from the 90s?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it, so the small current goes second

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly

explanation.surface: A tiny feed running on an old internet chat server.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts S and I after A GAS. Server suggests computing; Andre Agassi was a tennis champion of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi was a leading tennis player of the 1990s, and every tennis player serves.

clue.text: Terrible pain suing a terrible hospital

indicators.note: the second terrible says the letters before it are in a terrible state, so jumbled

parts.note: standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: The agony of taking a dreadful hospital to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering, a synonym for great pain.

clue.text: Little drinks making turn fall over

indicators.note: something that falls over ends up the other way round

explanation.surface: A few small drinks cause a dizzy spell and a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small measure of spirits, so nips are little drinks.

clue.text: Scuppering sailor takes bit of oomph in organising

indicators.note: the earlier pieces go inside the word that follows

parts.note: staging an event is organising it

indicators.note: only a small piece is used, the opening letter

explanation.surface: A sailor puts a bit of energy into organising, but the effort is wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor and the bit of oomph go in just after the first letter of the organising word.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck it deliberately, which is what sabotaging means.

clue.text: Note describing American hot dish

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the note encircles the rest

parts.note: the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, also written ti

explanation.surface: A note about a spicy American dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot dish' looks like one phrase; hot is H, and sushi is served cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or other toppings.

clue.text: More pleasant runs south of French resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed underneath

parts.note: a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Things are nicer once you run further south from the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning more agreeable or more pleasant.

clue.text: Jam-makers' parties filled with Welsh dowagers?

parts.note: the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation famed for jam-making

indicators.note: a thing filled with something holds it inside

explanation.surface: Women's Institute gatherings attended by elderly Welsh ladies.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title or property from her late husband, so dowagers are a kind of widow.

clue.text: Old beater driving hitcher around Britain

indicators.note: the mixed letters go around the abbreviation
driving the letters about sends them into a new order

explanation.surface: An old banger of a car driving a hitchhiker round Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old beater' suggests a battered old car; it is the cane once used for school beatings.
explanation.definitionFit: The birch was a bundle of twigs used to flog offenders, a punishment now abolished in Britain.

clue.text: Idiot Scotsman biting your tongue?

indicators.note: to bite is to hold between the teeth, so the other piece goes inside

explanation.surface: A foolish Scot biting your tongue for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiot and the Scotsman together bite the abbreviation between them. Assyrian is an ancient language of Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and Assyrian is one, a dialect of ancient Akkadian.

clue.text: Top soprano moving west in desire for drink

indicators.note: the letter shifts leftwards in an across answer and is set back in earlier

explanation.surface: A singer moving westward while longing for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The S in THIRST moves left, to sit after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is an upper-body garment, and a T-shirt is one kind.
